knowledge:
- key_parameters: maxGap=The maximum distance (in base pairs) between consecutive locations to be considered in the same cluster ;; cutoff=Numeric value (or two values) used to define the threshold for positive, near-zero, or negative segments ;; B=The number of resamples/permutations to run for creating a null distribution to assess uncertainty ;; X=The design matrix where one column represents the covariate of interest ;; permutation=User-supplied permutations to define the null distribution manually instead of using random permutations
- alternatives: charm=Preferred for preprocessing CHARM-like methylation microarrays before bump hunting ;; bsseq=Preferred for preprocessing whole-genome bisulfite sequencing data ;; minfi=Preferred for preprocessing Illumina 450k methylation arrays ;; limma=Uses lmFit for linear modeling of individual loci, whereas bumphunter is preferred when searching for contiguous genomic regions (bumps)
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing genomic data with several biological replicates (e.g., epigenomics, DNA methylation) where the goal is to identify contiguous genomic regions (bumps) associated with a covariate of interest, sharing information between nearby locations.
- pitfalls: When the design matrix X has columns other than the intercept and the covariate of interest (e.g., adjusting for confounders like age and sex), the permutation test approach is not recommended and will trigger a warning ;; Permutation testing with a large number of resamples (B) can be very slow, so registering a parallel backend using doParallel is highly recommended ;; Locations from different chromosomes must be separated, which is handled automatically by clusterMaker if chromosome names are provided.

workflows.name: region_finding_from_precomputed_coefficients
workflows.intent: Find and package genomic regions (bumps) from precomputed coefficients or test statistics without fitting a new statistical model.
input: chr (vector of chromosome names for each location)
beta1 (vector of precomputed coefficients or test statistics for each location)
workflows.stages: 1. Group genomic locations into clusters using clusterMaker ;; 2. Identify positive/negative segments using getSegments ;; 3. Find and tabulate regions using regionFinder
workflows.code:
pos <- list(pos1=seq(1,1000,35),
            pos2=seq(2001,3000,35),
            pos3=seq(1,1000,50))
chr <- rep(paste0("chr",c(1,1,2)), times = sapply(pos,length))
pos <- unlist(pos, use.names=FALSE)
cl <- clusterMaker(chr, pos, maxGap = 300)
table(cl)
Indexes <- split(seq_along(cl), cl)
beta1 <- rep(0, length(pos))
for(i in seq(along=Indexes)){
    ind <- Indexes[[i]]
    x <- pos[ind]
    z <- scale(x, median(x), max(x)/12)
    beta1[ind] <- i*(-1)^(i+1)*pmax(1-abs(z)^3,0)^3
}
segs <- getSegments(beta1, cl, cutoff=0.05)
tab <- regionFinder(beta1, chr, pos, cl, cutoff=0.05)

workflows.name: full_bumphunter_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a complete bump hunting analysis on a matrix of genomic measurements using a design matrix and permutation testing.
input: y (matrix of genomic measurements, e.g., methylation levels, where rows are locations and columns are samples)
X (design matrix with covariate of interest)
cl (vector of cluster IDs generated by clusterMaker)
workflows.stages: 1. Group genomic locations into clusters using clusterMaker ;; 2. Register parallel backend using doParallel for faster computation ;; 3. Run bumphunter to fit linear models, smooth coefficients, and perform permutation testing ;; 4. Clean up parallel connections using foreachCleanup
workflows.code:
cl <- clusterMaker(chr, pos, maxGap = 300)
beta0 <- 3*sin(2*pi*pos/720)
X <- cbind(rep(1,20), rep(c(0,1), each=10))
error <- matrix(rnorm(20*length(beta1), 0, 1), ncol=20)
y <- t(X[,1])%x%beta0 + t(X[,2])%x%beta1 + error
library(doParallel)
registerDoParallel(cores = 2)
tab <- bumphunter(y, X, chr, pos, cl, cutoff=.5, B=250, verbose = TRUE)
bumphunter:::foreachCleanup()
